chunks: My scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about bidding farewell to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: You say: 'May Allah bless you. Peace be upon you. May Allah not make this the last time I say peace to you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct supplication to recite when bidding farewell to the Prophet's grave?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the ritual etiquette of concluding a pilgrimage to the Prophet’s tomb with a specific supplication, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining a living spiritual connection with the Ahl al-Bayt. The phrase 'لا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ آخِرَ تَسْلِيمِي' (May Allah not make it my final greeting) underscores the hope for continued visitation and the enduring nature of the bond between the believer and the Prophet, a concept deeply rooted in Shia devotional practice.
